version.changelog:
Garden 1.1.4

- Improved security and consent language for all writing actions
- Now explicitly requires user confirmation before saving outside `~/garden/`
- Clarified that no preferences are inferred or saved without user approval
- Reinforced: no network calls, telemetry, or hardware control involved
- Changelog entry updated for transparency on these changes

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: garden
Version: 1.1.4

The OpenClaw Garden skill is designed for local data management, storing all information within a dedicated `~/garden/` directory. The `SKILL.md` and `setup.md` files explicitly state that the skill makes no external network calls, collects no telemetry, and does not write outside its designated directory without explicit user consent. The only shell commands identified (`mkdir -p ~/garden`, `touch ~/garden/memory.md` in `memory-template.md`) are for benign workspace setup. Instructions for the AI agent include strong guardrails against prompt injection, such as requiring explicit user consent for writing to the main `MEMORY.md` file and strictly limiting data saving to what the user explicitly shares. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence, or obfuscation was found.

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and low-risk because it operates locally and asks only to write garden files under ~/garden. Before installing or enabling integration: 1) Confirm how the skill will prompt you for the one-time consent to update your main MEMORY.md and what exact path it will write to; 2) Back up your existing MEMORY.md if you keep important data there; 3) If you expect the agent to handle photos, verify whether images are stored locally or uploaded (the SKILL.md says climate and photos are manual); 4) If you decline the workspace integration, the skill still functions locally — decline if you want to avoid cross-workspace writes. If you want extra assurance, ask the skill (or its author) to show the exact file operations it will perform during setup before granting consent.
